articles.title: Spring Bank Lane, roadworks in Rochdale on 12 November 2026
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council lists work affecting Spring Bank Lane in Rochdale; expected timings: 8am–6pm on Thursday, 12 November 2026.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has published a traffic notice for Spring Bank Lane in Rochdale. The council lists the expected start and finish as 8am–6pm on Thursday, 12 November 2026.

The council gives the reason as To install a sewer monitoring device. The notice describes the affected area as follows: Part of Spring Bank Lane will be temporarily closed.

The closure will begin 80 metres north of the junction with Bagslate Road and end a further 15 metres up the road in a northerly direction. No waiting will be allowed at any time in this section during the closure.

The published alternative route is There is no alternative route for vehicles. These are the details in the council's current published record, rather than confirmation that work has started or finished. Readers travelling through the area can check the original Rochdale Borough Council notice for any subsequent amendments.

articles.title: New transport policing command to cover Rochdale’s buses, trams and roads
articles.excerpt: A new Greater Manchester command brings transport and roads policing together, with more than 60 new officers announced across the network. No separate Rochdale allocation has been published.
articles.content_html:
People travelling on Rochdale’s buses, trams and roads will be covered by a new Greater Manchester policing command launched today, Thursday 29 October.

The Transport Policing and Crime Command brings Greater Manchester Police, Transport for Greater Manchester and the combined authority into a closer working structure to tackle crime, antisocial behaviour and dangerous driving across the transport network.

Chief Superintendent Suzanne Downey leads the command, which police describe as an effective 11th policing district alongside the region’s ten borough districts. The announcement includes more than 60 new officers across the network. It does not give a separate allocation for Rochdale or say how many additional patrols individual stops and routes will receive.

The command also incorporates the existing Roads Policing Unit, including specialist teams that investigate serious collisions and deal with commercial vehicles and motorcycle policing. New recruits are to be funded through additional mayoral investment, which police say will protect existing frontline resources.

Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson said: “TPACC represents a significant step forward in how we police and protect Greater Manchester's transport network.”

For Rochdale passengers, the practical question is whether closer coordination produces a more visible presence and quicker responses on the journeys they use. The announcement sets out those aims, rather than evidence that they have already been achieved.

The command’s roads teams have already operated in the borough. In a separate statement published on 3 September, police described stopping vehicles in Rochdale after reports of dangerous driving on the M66 and M62. That earlier operation is separate from today’s formal launch.

The new structure will work alongside TravelSafe LiveChat, which allows passengers to report concerns discreetly through the Bee Network app or QR codes on buses and trams. According to the launch release, more than 2,000 reports have been made through the service, with police responding to 800 incidents. Those are network-wide figures, not Rochdale totals.

Control room staff at police and TfGM will support the command using CCTV across the transport system. The plans also support Greater Manchester’s stated ambition to eliminate deaths and serious injuries on its roads by 2040.

Source: Greater Manchester Police’s launch release, supplied on 28 October under an embargo that expired at 6am on 29 October, and its published report of the September roads operation. No borough-specific staffing or incident figures were supplied.

articles.title: Rochdale Diversity Awards celebrate community contributions
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Diversity Awards, held on October 28, 2026, recognised individuals and organisations making a positive impact in the community, with MP Paul Waugh in attendance.
articles.content_html:
The Rochdale Diversity Awards took place on October 28, 2026, celebrating individuals and organisations that have made significant contributions to equality and community cohesion in Rochdale.

The event, organised by KYP since 2012, highlighted inspiring stories of local heroes who have worked to break down barriers and strengthen community ties.

Zulf Ahmed, a prominent figure in the community, described the awards as incredibly special, emphasising the importance of recognising those who help others thrive. The ceremony brought together community leaders and members, showcasing the best of Rochdale's efforts to promote diversity and inclusion.

Among the attendees was Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, who supported the initiative aimed at fostering a fairer and more inclusive environment in the borough. The awards not only acknowledge individual achievements but also aim to inspire others to contribute positively to the community.

The event is part of a broader initiative to promote diversity in Rochdale, encouraging ongoing efforts to create a more cohesive society. The next steps involve continuing to support and highlight the work of those dedicated to making a difference in the community.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Rochdale Diversity Awards Shine a Spotlight on Those Making a Difference - Rochdale Times Skip to content LATEST NEWS Rochdale Diversity Awards Shine a Spotlight on Those Making a Difference More than 350 guests came together at Rochdale Town Hall on Friday evening as the Rochdale Diversity Awards 2026 honoured the individuals and organisations transforming lives, creating opportunities and bringing communities together across the borough. Delivered by KYP (Kashmir Youth Project) since 2012, the awards recognised outstanding contributions to equality, diversity, inclusion and community cohesion. With finalists selected from more than 130 nominations, the evening showcased the very best of Rochdale and the people whose efforts make a positive difference every day. The evening brought together civic leaders, businesses, public sector organisations, charities, community groups and residents to celebrate the people and organisations whose dedication continues to break down barriers, create opportunities and strengthen communities. Zulf Ahmed, Chief Executive Officer of KYP, said: “The Rochdale Diversity Awards are about recognising the people and organisations whose commitment, compassion and leadership make a real difference to others every day. “This year we received more than 130 nominations, each telling a story of someone breaking down barriers, creating opportunities or helping others to thrive. Bringing together more than 350 guests to celebrate those achievements was incredibly special. Rochdale MP Paul Waugh with some of the winners. Image: Paul Waugh “The awards remind us of the strength of our communities and the extraordinary things that happen when people come together with a shared commitment to making Rochdale a fairer, more inclusive and more connected borough.” The audience also heard inspiring contributions from civic and community leaders from across the borough. Cllr Andy Kelly, Deputy Mayor of Rochdale, spoke of his pride in Rochdale’s diverse communities and reflected on how the borough’s rich mix of cultures, backgrounds and traditions continues to be one of its greatest strengths. Cllr Neil Emmott, Leader of Rochdale Borough Council, highlighted the importance of partnership and collective action in tackling inequality, strengthening communities and creating opportunities for residents across the borough. Elsie Blundell MP, Member of Parliament for Heywood and Middleton North, praised the generosity, resilience and community spirit she has witnessed across Rochdale, highlighting the importance of bringing people together, breaking down barriers and creating opportunities for everyone to succeed. READ MORE: New industrial units could inspire town’s entrepreneurs Julie Murphy, Chief Executive of Rochdale Council, said: “A truly inclusive community is one where nobody feels they have to leave part of themselves at the door to be accepted. We want every child and young person to believe they can succeed, regardless of their background or circumstances. “The finalists and winners we celebrate tonight are a powerful example of what can be achieved when we break down barriers, embrace diversity and create opportunities for everyone to thrive.” Paul Waugh MP, Member of Parliament for Rochdale and Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Early Education, said: “The people and organisations recognised tonight represent the very best of Rochdale. “Their dedication, compassion and commitment to helping others demonstrate the strength of our communities and the values that bring us together as a borough.” Mohammed (Attaur) Rahman, founder of Rochdale Science Initiative CIC, winner of the Breaking Barriers Award and Outstanding Achievement in Diversity Award, said: “Celebrating at the Rochdale Diversity Awards was a powerful reminder of what makes our borough special: its people, their resilience and their commitment to helping others thrive. Heywood and Middleton North MP Elsie Blundell with guests at the awards “These awards recognise the collective efforts of volunteers, community organisations and partners who work every day to create opportunities and remove barriers. It is an honour to be recognised alongside so many individuals and organisations making a meaningful difference across Rochdale.” Entertainment was provided by the K&K Queensway Royals Morris Dancing Troupe, which opened the evening with a vibrant performance reflecting the rich diversity and cultural heritage celebrated throughout the awards. The event was made possible through the generous support of Rochdale Boroughwide Housing, Altus Education Partnership, Rochdale Council, Your Trust, Hopwood Hall College, For Generations to Come, Ingeus, Harvest Touch Youth & Skills Community Hub, Greater Manchester High Sheriff’s Police Trust, Action Together and Rochdale Development Agency. The Rochdale Diversity Awards 2026 supported support Springhill Hospice as the event’s charity partner. Their dedication to providing outstanding care and support to patients and families across our communities reflects the values of compassion and service celebrated throughout the evening. The Rochdale Diversity Awards continue to recognise the individuals, community groups, employers, public services and voluntary organisations whose work strengthens communities, creates opportunities and helps make Rochdale a more inclusive borough. As planning begins for 2027, the awards remain an important celebration of the people whose efforts make a lasting difference to the lives of others across Rochdale. articles.title: Lachlan Lanskey joins Rochdale Hornets on one-year deal for 2027 season
articles.excerpt: Australia-born Ireland international Lachlan Lanskey has signed with Rochdale Hornets for the upcoming season after leaving Keighley Cougars.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Hornets have confirmed the signing of Lachlan Lanskey on a one-year deal for the 2027 season. The Australia-born Ireland international joins the club following his departure from Keighley Cougars, where he played for three years.

Lanskey, a back-rower, is a product of the Brisbane Broncos’ youth system and has represented Queensland at various youth levels.

Although he did not make an NRL appearance, he played for Brisbane Tigers in the Queensland Cup before moving to the UK in 2023 to join Whitehaven.

Currently, Lanskey represents Ireland internationally, having made his debut last autumn in a Test Series against Wales. He recently starred in a match against Scotland in the Celtic Cup, marking his third cap for the Wolfhounds.

Expressing his excitement about the move, Lanskey stated, “I’m really happy to be getting on board for the 2027 season.” His addition is expected to bolster Rochdale's squad as they prepare for the upcoming Championship campaign.
articles.social_headline: Lachlan Lanskey excited to join Rochdale Hornets for the 2027 season

articles.title: Scrooge screening with live orchestra comes to Heywood Civic
articles.excerpt: The 1951 film starring Alastair Sim will be shown with a live score from the three-piece FB Pocket Orchestra on Saturday 14 November.
articles.content_html:
A screening of the classic film Scrooge with a live three-piece orchestra is coming to Heywood Civic on Saturday 14 November.

The event starts at 8pm and pairs the 1951 film starring Alastair Sim with music performed by the FB Pocket Orchestra. The production is touring in the film’s 75th anniversary year.

The venue lists a running time of 90 minutes. Its Pay What You Can prices are £8.40 at the lower rate, £10.50 standard and £12.60 at the higher rate, all including the booking fee.

Rather than a stage adaptation, this is a showing of the film with live musical accompaniment. It follows Ebenezer Scrooge’s encounters with the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Future in the familiar Charles Dickens story.

The organisers say the music is based on Richard Addinsell’s original score. Heywood Civic’s listing explains that Paul Stevenson reconstructed the score by listening to and transcribing the film soundtrack, creating an arrangement for the ensemble.

The film has a U certificate. For local families and cinema fans, the event offers a chance to hear live musicians accompany a black-and-white Christmas classic at a borough venue.

Heywood Civic is on LCpl Stephen Shaw MC Way, Heywood, OL10 1LW. Tickets and the venue’s pricing information are available at https://heywoodcivic.co.uk/event/scrooge-u-live-to-film/. Check availability and the venue’s accessibility information before booking.

The event was announced in a press release supplied by FB Music and Media, with the date, running time and ticket prices checked against Heywood Civic’s listing on 28 October 2026.

articles.title: Newhouse Crescent, roadworks in Rochdale from 27 October 2026
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks on Newhouse Crescent will start on 27 October 2026, affecting local traffic for up to 21 days.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks on Newhouse Crescent will commence at 12 noon on Tuesday, 27 October 2026. The work is expected to last for a maximum of 21 days, or until the project is completed sooner.

The roadworks will result in a temporary closure of part of Newhouse Crescent, specifically 10 metres south of the junction with Inchfield Close, extending 10 metres further down the road in a southerly direction.

This closure will impact local traffic and may cause delays for residents and commuters in the area.

Residents and drivers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as access will be restricted during the roadworks. The council has provided a map of the roadworks and other restrictions across Greater Manchester for those needing to navigate around the affected area.

This development is significant for local residents and commuters, as it may affect daily travel routes and times. For more information on the roadworks and to view the map, visit the Rochdale Borough Council website.

articles.title: New industrial units planned at Caldershaw Business Centre in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Nine new industrial units are set to be built at Caldershaw Business Centre, aiming to boost local employment and support entrepreneurs.
articles.content_html:
Nine new industrial units are planned for construction at the Caldershaw Business Centre in Rochdale. The initiative aims to create jobs and provide opportunities for local entrepreneurs, according to a proposal submitted to Rochdale Council by Adil Iqbal of IQ7 Ltd.

The new units will occupy a previously disused area of land adjacent to Unit 6/5d at the business centre, which is located off Rooley Moor Road. The site, currently overgrown and littered, previously housed a mill building that has since been demolished.

The development is expected to transform this neglected space into a productive environment for new businesses.

Each of the nine units will range in size from 84 square metres to 164 square metres, featuring roller shutter doors, pedestrian access, small office spaces, and WC facilities.

The total industrial floor space will be approximately 1,170 square metres, providing a significant boost to local business infrastructure and potentially attracting new enterprises to the area.

The planning application is currently under review, with further updates anticipated as the project progresses. This development is significant as it aims to stimulate local entrepreneurship and job creation in Rochdale, addressing the need for more business space in the community.

A design and access statement submitted with the plans said: “The development aims to produce space for new businesses and potentially create jobs for members of the local community as well as opportunities for local entrepreneurs. “The land currently is disused, overgrown with vegetation and waste. The nine individual units range from 84sqm to 164sqm in size and each include a roller shutter door entrance with accompanying pedestrian access door, a small office and WC. “The site is currently vacant and is currently an underutilised parcel of land within an active employment area. articles.title: Construction milestone reached for Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: The Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre at Kingsway Business Park has completed its base build, marking a significant step in the development of Rochdale's advanced materials hub.
articles.content_html:
The Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale has reached a major milestone with the completion of its base build.

This development is part of the Atom Valley Innovation District, which aims to foster advanced materials and manufacturing innovation in the region.

Designed by Bond Bryan, the 30,000 sq. ft centre will serve as a vital link between research, specialist facilities, and commercial production.

It is expected to generate £107 million in economic value over the next decade, supporting the transition of new technologies from concept to commercial application.

The Rochdale Development Agency (RDA) has spearheaded the project in collaboration with the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), The University of Manchester, and other innovation partners. The next phase will focus on the fit-out of the centre, with operations anticipated to commence in 2027.

Mark Adey, director at Bond Bryan, highlighted the importance of creating environments that facilitate innovation and commercialisation. The SMMC is designed to adapt to emerging technologies and business needs, ensuring it remains relevant as industries evolve.

articles.title: Rochdale council deputy leader detained briefly in Pakistan during civic visit
articles.excerpt: Councillor Daalat Ali was held for a short time upon arrival in Pakistan as part of a delegation aimed at strengthening ties with Sahiwal.
articles.content_html:
Councillor Daalat Ali, the deputy leader of Rochdale council, was detained by authorities for a short period upon his arrival in Pakistan. This incident occurred during a civic delegation visit to the city of Sahiwal, which is twinned with Rochdale.

The delegation includes Rochdale's ceremonial mayor, Councillor Faisal Rana, and aims to strengthen relationships between the two areas, which have historical ties dating back to their twinning in 1998.

The council confirmed that the detention was brief and related to Councillor Ali's long-standing personal campaigning regarding the Kashmir region. A spokesperson for the council stated that such detentions are not uncommon for individuals travelling to this region, particularly those with political views.

Councillor Ali is reported to be safe and well, having continued his travels and meetings with local officials after the incident.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office also acknowledged the situation, confirming that they were in contact with local authorities regarding the matter.

While the exact reasons for Councillor Ali's detention have not been officially confirmed by Pakistani authorities, the council's statement reassured that he was able to resume his duties as part of the delegation shortly thereafter.

This visit is significant for Rochdale, as many residents have familial connections to Sahiwal.

The delegation's activities include attending various events, such as the opening of a Sewing Machine Centre by the Al-Mahmood Foundation, which is part of the ongoing efforts to foster community ties and support local initiatives in both regions.

articles.title: Rochdale’s Deckers Hospitality Group acquires historic drinks wholesaler Tate-Smith
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale-based family group has bought the Malton drinks wholesaler, with existing staff staying and Harry Tate-Smith continuing as trading director.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale-based Deckers Hospitality Group has acquired North Yorkshire drinks wholesaler Tate-Smith, adding a business founded in 1888 to its portfolio.

The deal brings together two family businesses. Deckers is led by siblings Max Brierley and Victoria Cosgrove and operates in hospitality, wholesale and e-commerce.

Tate-Smith, based in Malton, supplies soft and alcoholic drinks across North Yorkshire. The business had been owned by the same family for six generations.

According to the announcement issued on 22 October, it will continue trading as Tate-Smith Ltd. All current staff will remain, and Harry Tate-Smith will continue in the business as trading director.

Paul and Cate Tate-Smith sold the company. Paul said the time was right to pass it to a business that could support its next stage, while retaining a role for their son.

Maxwell Brierley, of Deckers Hospitality Group, said: “Like us Tate-Smith is a family-run business with an impressive history. We felt it was the perfect fit for us as we continue to develop and grow our portfolio, and we welcome them to our family.”

For Rochdale, the acquisition marks an expansion of a locally based group into an established Yorkshire wholesale business. The release does not disclose a purchase price or announce any additional Rochdale jobs.

AAB and Schofield Sweeney advised Tate-Smith’s shareholders. Deckers was advised by Pannone Corporate and Cowgills, part of the Sumer Group.

Source: a press release supplied by The Right Agency on behalf of the advisers, first sent on 22 October 2026 and followed up on 28 October. What would you like to see Rochdale’s hospitality businesses invest in next? Share your views in the comments.

articles.title: Heywood lollipop man forced to leap out of way as drivers ignore crossing
articles.excerpt: A car and a moped have been seized after their drivers failed to stop for a lollipop man in Heywood, forcing him to jump aside for safety.
articles.content_html:
A car and a moped have been seized by Greater Manchester Police after their drivers ignored a lollipop man in Heywood, forcing him to leap out of the way on two separate occasions. The incidents occurred on Bury Old Road on 13 and 14 October, as reported by Rochdale Borough Council.

Barry Jones, the lollipop man involved, was standing in the road when both vehicles failed to stop. The council noted that there have been 137 reported incidents of drivers not stopping for school crossing patrols across the borough in the last five years, highlighting a concerning trend regarding road safety near schools.

Following the incidents, police gathered evidence, including witness statements, which led to the seizure of the silver Skoda car and the moped.

A recent change in law, effective from June, allows police to seize vehicles without issuing a warning first under the Police Reform Act 2002.

Dylan Williams, the cabinet member for highways, expressed gratitude to the police for their prompt action and stated that the council would continue to report such incidents and pursue prosecutions where possible.

This situation underscores the importance of road safety, particularly in school zones, and the need for drivers to adhere to traffic regulations.
